title: The Effect of Minimum Wage on Employment
abstract: This paper examines the causal impact of minimum wage increases on employment levels using a difference-in-differences approach. We find modest negative effects on teen employment.

title: Monetary Policy and Asset Prices
abstract: We develop a DSGE model to analyze how monetary policy shocks affect asset prices. Our results suggest that interest rate changes have significant effects on equity valuations.

title: Trade Liberalization and Income Inequality
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between trade openness and income distribution using panel data from 50 countries over 30 years. We find heterogeneous effects across skill groups.

title: Behavioral Responses to Carbon Taxation
abstract: We estimate the elasticity of gasoline demand with respect to carbon taxes using Swedish administrative data. Our estimates suggest a price elasticity of approximately -0.3.

title: Machine Learning for Causal Inference
abstract: This paper surveys recent advances in using machine learning methods for causal inference in economics. We discuss LASSO for variable selection and random forests for heterogeneous treatment effects.

title: The Long-Run Effects of Education Quality
abstract: Using historical school construction data we estimate the returns to education quality. A one standard deviation improvement in teacher quality increases lifetime earnings by 8 percent.

title: Housing Markets and Spatial Equilibrium
abstract: We develop a quantitative spatial model of housing markets with heterogeneous agents. The model explains 70 percent of the variation in house prices across US metropolitan areas.

title: Firm Dynamics and Aggregate Productivity
abstract: This paper documents facts about firm entry exit and growth using Census microdata. We find that declining business dynamism accounts for half of the productivity slowdown since 2000.

title: Optimal Unemployment Insurance Design
abstract: We characterize the optimal unemployment insurance policy in a model with moral hazard and liquidity constraints. The optimal replacement rate is around 50 percent.

title: Network Effects in Technology Adoption
abstract: Using data on social networks and smartphone adoption we estimate peer effects in technology diffusion. A 10 percentage point increase in friend adoption raises own adoption by 3 points.
